issues.failure_explanation: The proofs use L_reg(u_θ*) ≤ L(θ*) and L_bc(θ*) ≤ L(θ*), which require L_ent(u_θ*) ≥ 0. This is never shown and can fail. If v > c everywhere, then sgn(v−k_h)=1 for every k_h in V_h^c, so L_ent(v)=∫∇·F(v), which can be negative (e.g. ∂_t v<0). No a priori bound keeps u_θ* within [−c,c]. Without these inequalities, neither the O(1) bound on ∫|∇·F(u_θ*)| used in the strip selection nor the initial-error bound follows.

issues.failure_explanation: In a compound wave the shock is attached to the fan, so its rarefaction-side trace has gradients of size ~1/t near the origin. The single-shock argument needs uniform W^{2,∞} one-sided states to get the pointwise shift bound O(Mh), and the paper itself states this bound fails for singular one-sided states (shock-birth appendix). The omitted proof is therefore nontrivial. The claimed rate (h|ln h|)^{1/2} also conflicts with the O(h^{1/2}|ln h|) used for compound waves in the main proof.
